speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my clinic. I understand you are suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bouts of bronchitis; to begin our assessment, how long has the cough been present, and do you produce any sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the 11-year duration of a chronic cough with copious yellow-green sputum in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of Bronchiectasis. To confirm this, have you ever been told that your lungs look "damaged" or that you've had blood in your cough? REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_High_Resolution.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No other significant past medical history aside from the recurrent bronchitis. Social history: Non-smoker, no history of alcohol or drug abuse.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, weight loss, night sweats, or shortness of breath. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

The history of an 11-year chronic cough with copious purulent sputum in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of a specific structural lung disease. I will proceed with a high-resolution CT scan to visualize airway dilation and confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_High_Resolution

speaker: Doctor
text:
The "normal readings" provided do not clarify the specific nature of your lung structure. Given your 11-year history of chronic cough with copious purulent sputum in a non-smoker, I need to visualize your airways to rule out or confirm bronchiectasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very strange; a CT_Chest_High_Resolution scan should definitively show airway dilation if bronchiectasis were present, yet it returned normal readings. Since you are a non-smoker with an 11-year history of copious purulent sputum, could this be an allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) or a primary ciliary dyskinesia? Have you ever had an allergic reaction to fungi, or does your sputum ever contain dark plugs? REQUEST TEST: Total_IgE.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have reviewed your normal High-Resolution CT scan; since structural damage like bronchiectasis is ruled out, your long-term symptoms of copious purulent sputum and recurrent bronchitis in a non-smoker suggest an infectious or immunologic etiology. Have you noticed any wheezing, particularly when you expectorate, and do you have a history of asthma or known allergies? REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture_and_Sensitivity; REQUEST TEST: Total_IgE.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sputum_Culture: Heavy growth of non-specific bacteria, no TB or fungal growth.; Total_IgE: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis. The clinical picture of an 11-year history of daily productive cough with purulent sputum in a non-smoker, combined with a normal High-Resolution CT (ruling out bronchiectasis) and normal IgE (making ABPA unlikely), meets the classic definition of chronic bronchitis.
